newsitem.title: USA: SEC sanctions Salomon over accounting errors.
newsitem.headline: SEC sanctions Salomon over accounting errors.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said on Wednesday that it issued a cease and desist order against Salomon Inc for errors and inaccuracies that were included in its books from possibly the mid-1980s through 1994.
Salomon, one of Wall Street's largest investment banking firms, consented to the order without admitting or denying any wrongdoing, the SEC said.
In accepting Salomon's settlement offer, the SEC said considered remedies promptly undertaken by Salomon and the cooperation it extended in SEC's inquiry into the matter.

The SEC, in an administrative proceeding, said Salomon discovered it overstated assets and income in its books from at least 1989, and possibly as early as 1984, through 1994 in a management-initiated review of internal accounting controls.
The SEC said the review was begun in 1992 and completed in 1993 for the firm's domestic subsidiaries, and in 1994 for its unit, Salomon Brothers Holding Company Inc and London-based subsidiaries.
As a result of the review, Salomon ultimately wrote off unreconciled balances in general accounts, which were disclosed in an annual report filed for 1994, the SEC said.

Salomon, in its 1994 annual report, noted that, with the exception of the fourth quarter of 1994, the impact on earnings of certain charges taken as a result of unreconciled balances and accounting problems was not material in any single period, the SEC said.

The SEC said it found Salomon's internal accounting controls between 1984 and 1994 were inadequate to prevent, detect or correct unreconciled balances disclosed in the 1994 report. For example, a review by Salomon of its London-based companies showed several hundred accounts were not properly reconciled for several years. The failure to reconcile balance sheet accounts properly also occurred at other Salomon subsidiaries, the SEC said.
